main_text.p: tentus. IX. Anthypophora est, cùm vnum argumentum conceditur, opposito fortiori. Dicitur alio nomine ἀντι-καταλλάξις & ἀντεισαγωγὴ, compensatio. Exemplum insigne est Matth. 21. vers. 23. 24. 25. vbi Christus Pharisæis quærentibus, Quâ potestate hoc facis? respondet, Interrogabo [?]& ego vos quiddam: Baptismus Iohannis vnde erat? ex cœlo an ex hominibus?

XIX. Actio est ornata elocutionis prolatio; conueniente scil. voce & gestu. Vox conueniens est, quæ debitam habet quantitatem & qualitatem. Ratione 10 quantitatis vox est intensa & remissa, item tarda, distincta, expedita, & denique firma, non decrescens, sed sæpe augescens. Ratione qualitatis vox est exilis, flebilis, ex-ultans, aspera, acuta, grauis, horrida, suauis &c. Vtro-bique oportet vt vocis sonus sit accommodatus rebus.15 Sic in miseratione debet esse vox flebilis, flexibilis, ple-na, & interrupta: in iracundia, acuta, incitata, & cre-bro incidens: in metu & verecundia, contracta, hæsi-tans, & lenta: in dolore grauis, pressa & lachrymabilis: in risu & lætitia, clara-pura, & exultans. Esa.58.verf.1.Dan.20 6.verf.21.Iud.8.verf.1.& feqq. 2.Reg. 18. v.28. Matth. 23. per to-tum. Gestus conueniens est, qui rebus, affectibus, voci, & consuetudini est accommodatus. Sic demissio capitis est habitus conueniens luctui, dolori, & humiliationi Esa.58. v.5. Oculi in aliquem conuersi indicant captationem at-25tentionis Luc.6.v.20. Lachrymæ indicant mœrorem. Luc. 19.v.41. Percussio pectoris & deiectio oculorum est signum humilitatis. Luc.18.ver.13. Vide infra Ciuilem conuersationem.30

page.notes: The Greek word after "alio nomine" is printed across a line break ("ἀντι-" / "καταλλάξις"); the Greek letters and accents are copied as far as readable, with [?] where unsure. The sign after "Interrogabo" is an unclear symbol, marked [?]. The marginal "10" is read as printed. The Greek "ἀντεισαγωγὴ" is uncertain in its accents. The large initial L is joined to "Ogica" as printed. Marginal numbers 15 to 35 are printed line numbers. The word "sacræ" is doubtful, its long s may be an f.
